name: Oslo - P for Plastic
shortDescription: OSLO-P carries Oslo's fine line texture onto interior plastic panels, useful for acrylic dividers and shields.
description:
OSLO-P adapts the restrained Oslo line pattern for compatible interior plastic surfaces, giving acrylic or polycarbonate panels a fine frosted texture instead of a bare utility look. Light still passes through the panel, but direct view-through becomes softer and more finished.

In Philadelphia, that matters for Center City tenant suites, University City clinics, and retail counters where acrylic dividers sit near glass conference fronts or sidelites. The film helps those plastic panels feel intentional, especially when the surrounding space already uses 3M Fasara finishes.

This is a decorative finish, so expectations should center on privacy, diffusion, and appearance rather than solar heat control. Plastic substrates need careful review because cleaning habits, panel flex, and edge exposure differ from standard architectural glass.

Choose OSLO-P when the project includes plastic panels. Standard Oslo is the better match for true glass, while OSLO-P is the variant that keeps the same quiet design language on approved plastic surfaces.

benefits.heading: Plastic Compatibility
benefits.body: This version is intended for interior plastic substrates where standard glass films may not be appropriate.

benefits.heading: Light Management
benefits.body: The finish adds privacy and diffusion while keeping the panel useful as part of the interior design.

name: Oslo
shortDescription: OSLO's Nordic line grid gives office glass a crisp architectural screen without heavy frost or cloudiness.
description:
OSLO uses fine linear geometry to create a calm, architectural frost that reads more like woven structure than plain white film. Daylight stays clean and even, while the pattern breaks up faces, movement, and desk-level clutter behind the glass.

It is a strong fit for Center City coworking partitions, Old City studio doors, and conference fronts in converted Philadelphia buildings where glass needs privacy without making narrow rooms feel closed off. The restrained linework pairs well with brick, wood, black metal, and modern tenant finishes.

From inside and outside, OSLO looks patterned rather than opaque; people close to the glass may still register as softened shapes. It should be cleaned like a finished interior surface and specified with attention to band height, viewing distance, and alignment.

Choose OSLO over Dusted Crystal when the glass needs a recognizable design detail. Choose Privacy Matte when the priority is simpler obscuration with less visible pattern.

benefits.heading: Privacy Control
benefits.body: The pattern interrupts direct sightlines while allowing useful daylight to move through the glass.

benefits.heading: Design Upgrade
benefits.body: It gives plain glass a finished architectural surface without replacing the pane or ordering custom glass.

benefits.heading: Flexible Application
benefits.body: The film works well for offices, retail, healthcare, hospitality, and residential interior glass.

name: Opaque White
shortDescription: Opaque White creates full privacy on Philadelphia glass with solid white face. without replacing glass.
description:
With solid white face that fully obscures views while still looking clean and architectural, Opaque White solves a narrower glass problem than a standard tint. It is selected when partial privacy, dots, gradients, or soft frost would still reveal too much. The finish turns transparent glass into an intentional opaque design surface.

In Philadelphia, this can help Center City clinics, salons, retail back walls, media rooms, and back-of-house partitions control what is visible from public areas. It is also useful when a tenant inherits glass that no longer matches the way the room is used.

The product is decorative and privacy-focused, not a solar-performance film. Its value comes from view control, consistent appearance, and the ability to change glass behavior without replacing the lite. For privacy-critical areas, that directness is often the point.

Choose Opaque White instead of a translucent Fasara pattern when the project needs full obscuration. Choose a matte or crystal Fasara film when daylight transmission and a softer privacy effect are still part of the design brief. Full privacy products require more careful placement than decorative films that simply blur the view. In Philadelphia commercial interiors, Opaque White is strongest where the glass should function as a clean visual stop: storage rooms, treatment areas, display backers, private offices, or back-of-house transitions. It can also solve awkward retrofit conditions where a tenant inherited too much glass for the current use of the room. Instead of covering the pane with blinds or temporary signage, this 3M film gives the surface a permanent-looking design decision that can still be changed later.

benefits.heading: Full Obscuration
benefits.body: The finish stops view-through where partial privacy is not enough.

benefits.heading: Clean Surface
benefits.body: A matte face gives glass a deliberate, finished look rather than an improvised covering.

benefits.heading: Interior Flexibility
benefits.body: It can define back-of-house areas, media zones, displays, and private rooms without new glazing.

name: Neutral 70 (Re70Nearl) - Sun Control Film
shortDescription: At 70% VLT, Neutral 70 tempers glare while keeping Philadelphia glass 70% VLT neutral tone that reads almost clear.
description:
For glass needing 70% VLT neutral tone that reads almost clear from the sidewalk, Neutral 70 (Re70Nearl) - Sun Control Film brings a deliberate 3M finish to Philadelphia interiors. It belongs in the 3M Sun Control Series, so the main decision is how much visible light and privacy the room can trade for heat and glare relief. The 70% option gives this page its character: lighter versions keep a near-clear appearance, while darker versions make sun control more obvious from inside.

In Philadelphia, Neutral 70 (Re70Nearl) - Sun Control Film is a practical fit for University City properties, west-facing rowhomes, and commercial glass along Market Street or the Schuylkill where afternoon sun can make rooms hard to use. Climate Zone 4A brings humid summers and cold winters, so a solar film must improve comfort without creating an exterior look that conflicts with historic districts, HOA rules, or building management standards.

Technically, this product is selected around 70% visible light transmission, moderate heat rejection, and over 99% UV rejection. It is not a blackout film or a decorative frost; it is a solar-control specification for glass where the occupants still want daylight, views, and a cleaner neutral appearance. Final glass compatibility depends on pane type, orientation, and existing shade conditions.

Choose Neutral 70 (Re70Nearl) - Sun Control Film over lighter Sun Control films when glare or privacy has become more important than maximum brightness. Choose a lighter 3M Neutral product when the project is in Society Hill, Old City, or Chestnut Hill and the glass needs to look almost unchanged from the street.

benefits.heading: Solar Comfort
benefits.body: The film reduces solar intensity at the glass, helping rooms stay more usable during Philadelphia summer afternoons.

benefits.heading: Glare Control
benefits.body: Its visible light level is selected to cut screen glare without making the space feel unnecessarily closed in.

benefits.heading: UV Protection
benefits.body: The construction blocks over 99% of UV exposure, helping protect floors, displays, art, and furnishings.

name: Anti Graffiti 6 (AG-6)
shortDescription: Anti Graffiti 6 (AG-6) adds a clear 6 mil sacrificial layer for Philadelphia glass exposed to scratches and tagging.
description:
For glass needing clear 6 mil sacrificial layer with more abuse tolerance than AG-4, Anti Graffiti 6 (Ag-6) brings a deliberate 3M finish to Philadelphia interiors. The important specification is thickness: 6 mil clear polyester gives the glass a replaceable wear layer rather than changing the look of the storefront or interior partition.

This matters in Philadelphia where SEPTA-adjacent storefronts, Center City vestibules, elevators, schools, and restaurant glass can see scratches, etching, stickers, and marker damage. Instead of replacing expensive glass after surface damage, property teams can replace the sacrificial film layer.

Anti Graffiti 6 (Ag-6) is optically clear, privacy-neutral, and not primarily a heat-control product. It protects the surface from routine abuse and helps preserve appearance, but it should not be described as making glass vandal-proof or unbreakable.

Choose Anti Graffiti 6 (Ag-6) when the risk is surface damage rather than solar discomfort. AG-6 is the heavier option for higher-traffic or repeat-damage locations; AG-4 is better when the goal is a lighter protective layer for routine maintenance planning. The 6 mil construction should be matched to the surface-risk level, not treated as a one-size-fits-all product. A busy storefront near transit may justify a heavier sacrificial layer, while interior glass in a school, clinic, or lobby may need a cleaner maintenance-focused specification. Because this is clear anti-graffiti film, the best result is almost invisible until the glass is damaged. That makes Anti Graffiti 6 (Ag-6) useful for Philadelphia property teams that want a practical maintenance plan without changing storefront transparency, tenant branding, or the look of the surrounding facade.

benefits.body: The film takes the scratches, etching, and marker damage so the underlying glass can stay intact.

shortDescription: Illumina P (For Plastic) brings Fasara texture to Philadelphia acrylic panels with gradation pattern made for.
description:
With gradation pattern made for plastic panels instead of glass, Illumina P (For Plastic) solves a narrower glass problem than a standard tint. The key differentiator is substrate compatibility: it is intended for interior plastic panels, not just standard architectural glass. That matters for modern buildouts with acrylic dividers or modular partitions.

Philadelphia offices, clinics, and retail spaces in University City often mix glass with acrylic panels, especially in renovated tenant suites. This product lets those plastic surfaces coordinate with nearby Fasara glass finishes instead of looking like an afterthought.

Because it is decorative, the performance conversation is about privacy, diffusion, and finish rather than heat rejection. It can soften view-through and add a designed texture while maintaining a lighter, more integrated interior feel.

Choose Illumina P (For Plastic) when the project includes plastic substrates. If the same visual character is needed on true glass, the non-P version in the Fasara family is usually the better match. Plastic compatibility is important because acrylic and polycarbonate panels behave differently than architectural glass. For Philadelphia tenant improvements, that can mean using Illumina P (For Plastic) on reception shields, modular dividers, or display panels while nearby glass receives a related Fasara finish. The goal is continuity: the eye reads one designed interior system instead of a mix of bare plastic and finished glass. Window Film Philadelphia can evaluate the substrate, edge conditions, and cleaning expectations before recommending this plastic-specific 3M option. For local projects, the final recommendation should account for glass size, viewing angle, existing interior finishes, and how much privacy occupants need during daytime and evening use. That review keeps Illumina P (For Plastic) tied to the room instead of treating it as a generic catalog selection.

It is useful for Philadelphia conference rooms, reception glass, and restaurant entries where the lower portion of a pane needs screening while the upper area should stay open. The white gradient keeps the look quiet and luminous.

Gradient placement is the key practical detail: the dense portion should align with the sightline that needs coverage. The film is decorative, so it should not be selected for solar heat control.

Choose Illumina Silky W for a soft white transition. Illumina Silver is more reflective and metallic, while standard matte films provide uniform privacy across the whole pane.

name: Chamonix
shortDescription: Chamonix 2 deepens the alpine frost effect, giving glass more texture and privacy than Chamonix.
description:
Chamonix 2 builds on the delicate alpine frost character of Chamonix with a denser, more private read. The pattern feels natural and crystalline, giving the glass texture without turning it into a plain white panel.

Philadelphia spas, healthcare rooms, and residential bath glass can use this version when the lighter Chamonix leaves too much visible. It also works in hospitality areas where privacy should feel softer than a flat matte finish.

The denser frost reduces detail and movement more than Chamonix, though lighting and distance still affect what can be seen. Samples should be evaluated where privacy expectations are strict.

Choose Chamonix 2 when the same alpine character needs more coverage. Choose Chamonix for lighter diffusion, or Privacy Matte for a simpler, more uniform privacy layer.

name: Chamonix
shortDescription: Chamonix layers delicate alpine frost across glass, adding light diffusion with a refined texture.
description:
Chamonix gives glass a delicate alpine frost character, with a light textured surface that suggests ice crystals rather than flat opacity. It diffuses light gently and adds a refined pattern to otherwise plain panes.

It fits Philadelphia rowhome bathrooms, boutique office doors, and hospitality sidelites where privacy is useful but the design should remain light. The pattern works well when a project wants something more memorable than standard matte frost.

Close shapes can still appear as softened movement, particularly when backlit. The film should be selected for subtle texture and diffusion, not for full concealment.

Choose Chamonix for the lighter version of this look. Chamonix 2 is denser and more private, while Luce is airier with less pattern presence.

name: Dusted Crystal
shortDescription: Dusted Crystal gives glass a fine sandblasted look, a neutral choice for doors, logos, and sidelites.
description:
Dusted Crystal creates a fine sandblasted appearance that feels familiar, neutral, and clean. It changes clear glass into an etched-looking surface without the heavier whiteness of some privacy mattes.

Philadelphia uses include historic front door sidelites, office logos, restaurant glass, and residential baths where a classic frosted look is needed. It works across many interiors because it does not introduce a strong pattern or color.

The film diffuses view-through and can be used as full coverage, bands, or cut graphics depending on the design. Cleaning should be gentle so the finished surface keeps its clear etched appearance.

Choose Dusted Crystal for a versatile etched-glass effect. Mat Crystal 1 is flatter and more architectural, while Milky Crystal adds a softer glow.

name: Ceilo - Dot
shortDescription: Ceilo-Dot floats tiny dots across glass for an airy graphic layer with lighter privacy.
description:
Ceilo-Dot uses small, light dot geometry that appears to float across the pane. It adds a graphic layer without making the glass feel dense, so the room stays bright and visually open.

It is a good fit for Philadelphia retail entries, coworking spaces, and student-facing offices where glass needs visibility markers and light screening. The pattern feels playful but still clean enough for professional interiors.

The privacy level is lighter than denser dot films; it interrupts sightlines but leaves the room readable. Dot scale and spacing should be checked against mullions, door rails, and hardware.

Choose Ceilo-Dot when the project needs airiness. Kanon-Dot is more regular and precise, Luna 6-Dot is more rhythmic, and Aura 9-Dot creates a denser presence.

name: Black Blockout Matte Film
shortDescription: Black Blockout Matte Film creates full privacy on Philadelphia glass with black matte blackout surface.
description:
Where plain glass needs black matte blackout surface that stops view-through, Black Blockout Matte Film gives designers a controlled film option. It is selected when partial privacy, dots, gradients, or soft frost would still reveal too much. The finish turns transparent glass into an intentional opaque design surface.

In Philadelphia, this can help Manayunk clinics, salons, retail back walls, media rooms, and back-of-house partitions control what is visible from public areas. It is also useful when a tenant inherits glass that no longer matches the way the room is used.

The product is decorative and privacy-focused, not a solar-performance film. Its value comes from view control, consistent appearance, and the ability to change glass behavior without replacing the lite. For privacy-critical areas, that directness is often the point.

Choose Black Blockout Matte Film instead of a translucent Fasara pattern when the project needs full obscuration. Choose a matte or crystal Fasara film when daylight transmission and a softer privacy effect are still part of the design brief. Full privacy products require more careful placement than decorative films that simply blur the view. In Philadelphia commercial interiors, Black Blockout Matte Film is strongest where the glass should function as a clean visual stop: storage rooms, treatment areas, display backers, private offices, or back-of-house transitions. It can also solve awkward retrofit conditions where a tenant inherited too much glass for the current use of the room. Instead of covering the pane with blinds or temporary signage, this 3M film gives the surface a permanent-looking design decision that can still be changed later.

name: Aura 9 - Dot
shortDescription: Aura 9-Dot clusters nine dots for a denser prism sparkle with stronger presence than lighter dot films.
description:
Aura 9-Dot uses clustered nine-dot geometry to create a denser prism effect across the glass. It catches light with more sparkle and presence than smaller or more widely spaced dot patterns.

Philadelphia creative offices, boutique storefronts, and hospitality partitions can use Aura 9-Dot when the glass should feel energetic and visible. It makes a stronger design statement while still preserving some transparency.

Privacy is pattern-based rather than opaque; the denser clusters disrupt views but do not fully hide activity. Installation layout should account for repeat, hardware, and how the pattern meets pane edges.

Choose Aura 9-Dot when dot films need more visual strength. Ceilo-Dot is airier, Kanon-Dot is more precise, and Luna 6-Dot has a softer rhythmic grouping.

name: Astral Silver-Prism
shortDescription: Astral Silver-Prism scatters light with a geometric shimmer, turning interior glass into a bright accent.
description:
Astral Silver-Prism combines a silver tone with prism geometry, so light catches and scatters across the glass. The finish has a reflective shimmer that feels more dimensional than a plain dot or frost pattern.

It suits Philadelphia hospitality spaces, creative offices, and boutique retail displays where glass should become a visual accent. Used on feature panes or privacy bands, it can add movement without adding color.

The shimmer changes with lighting and viewing angle, so it should be reviewed in the actual room if consistency is important. It provides decorative screening, not the predictable opacity of matte privacy film.

Choose Astral Silver-Prism when sparkle and geometry are the point. Illumina Silver is a smoother gradient, and Aura 9-Dot gives dot density without the same prism sheen.

name: DI-NOC Architectural Finishes
shortDescription: 3M DI-NOC Architectural Finishes transform walls, doors, columns, and furniture with 900+ patterns — wood, stone, metal, leather, and abstract — at a fraction of the cost of full material replacement.
description:
3M DI-NOC Architectural Finishes are surface films, not window films — they transform existing interior surfaces with realistic material aesthetics that would otherwise require full demolition and replacement. Applied to walls, columns, doors, cabinetry, countertops, elevator cabs, and furniture, DI-NOC uses 3M's Comply Adhesive technology to wrap flat, curved, and complex 3D surfaces with virtually no air bubbles and a precise, professional finish.

With over 900 patterns across 23+ categories — fine wood, metallic, stone, leather, textile, carbon fiber, high gloss, and more — DI-NOC is specified on Philadelphia commercial renovation projects where a material change is needed but demolition, downtime, and construction cost make traditional replacement impractical. A Center City law firm can update the wood-panel look of a reception wall in a day. A hospitality property can re-skin elevator interiors without taking the cab out of service for weeks. A healthcare facility can refresh corridor walls without generating construction waste or disrupting patient areas.

DI-NOC uses 3M Comply Adhesive, which contains a micro-channel structure that channels air out during installation — a technology that makes large-surface applications significantly faster and more consistent than traditional surface films. The film is resistant to common stains, cleaners, and disinfectants, making it suitable for healthcare and foodservice environments.

Window Film Philadelphia installs DI-NOC as part of comprehensive renovation projects — often alongside 3M Fasara glass finishes, solar control film, or safety film — for a coordinated interior treatment across all surfaces in the space.

benefits.body: Fine wood, stone, metallic, leather, textile, carbon fiber, and abstract finishes available — enough design range to match any Philadelphia interior program from a single supplier.

benefits.body: DI-NOC transforms existing surfaces without demolition, construction waste, or extended closure — applied directly over existing painted walls, laminates, metal panels, and most interior substrates.
